title: The Force Lab
summary: Steer charges and wires in magnetic fields: force direction, force on a wire, circles and helices.
subject: physics
concepts: Circular motion in a magnetic field
learningOutcome: The student can find the direction and size of the force on a moving charge or a wire in a magnetic field, and the radius, frequency and pitch of the path of a charge in a uniform field.

levels.title: Which way is the push?
levels.adds: Baseline: the force F = qv × B is perpendicular to v and B and reverses for a negative charge (Example 4.2).
hints: The force is perpendicular to both the velocity and the field.
Use the right-hand rule for a positive charge: fingers along v, curl towards B, thumb along F.
For an electron, reverse the direction. With v perpendicular to B, F = qvB.

levels.title: Force on a wire
levels.adds: New idea: F = BIl sin θ for a wire, and balancing it against weight (Ex 4.5, 4.6, Example 4.1).
hints: Only the component of the field across the wire matters: B sin θ.
Change the length to metres and give the answer in the unit asked for.
To hold a wire up, the magnetic force BIl must equal mg.

levels.title: Round and round
levels.adds: New idea: the force supplies the centripetal force, so r = mv/qB and f = qB/2πm (Ex 4.11, 4.12, Example 4.3).
hints: The frequency is qB/2πm: speed does not appear.
1 G = 10⁻⁴ T. Give r in cm and f in MHz.

levels.title: Faster electron
levels.adds: Misconception check: a faster electron circles on a bigger circle in the same time (Ex 4.12).
hints: The radius is proportional to the speed.
Look at the formula for the frequency: is the speed in it?
A bigger circle at a higher speed takes the same time per circuit.

levels.title: The helix
levels.adds: More steps: split the velocity along and across the field; r from the cross part, pitch from the along part.
hints: The component across the field is v sin θ and sets the radius.
The component along the field is v cos θ and carries the electron forward.
Pitch = v cos θ × the period T = 2πm/qB.

misconceptions: The magnetic force acts along the direction of the velocity
A faster charge takes less time to go round its circle
A magnetic field speeds the particle up
An electron and a proton are pushed the same way
